title: Bar Chart vs Line Chart Selection Rules
description: Fundamental chart selection rules between discrete categorical comparisons and continuous temporal trends.
conditions: Displaying metric values across independent categories or chronological time points
Ensuring honest visual encoding that does not imply false continuity
recommended_methods: Horizontal Bar Chart for unordered categorical comparisons with long labels
Vertical Bar Chart (Column Chart) for small number of categories (< 7) or ordinal sequences
Line Chart with continuous chronological x-axis
selection_rules: NEVER use a Line Chart for discrete, unordered categories (connecting unrelated categories implies false interpolation)
ALWAYS start the numerical axis at ZERO (0) for Bar Charts to prevent visual distortion of ratio quantities
Use Line Charts strictly when the x-axis represents a continuous, ordered dimension (time, distance, age)
limitations: Starting y-axis at zero on line charts can compress subtle, meaningful variations (zoomed y-axis is permissible on line charts if labeled)
Stacked bar charts become difficult to read for intermediate segments (use 100% stacked or faceted bars)
